subject: psychology
intro: Psychology leads to work with minds and behaviour — clinicians treating distress, psychologists shaping schools and workplaces, psychiatrists prescribing, and analysts testing what people buy.

roles.title: Clinical and Counseling Psychologists
roles.what: Assess, diagnose and treat mental and emotional disorders through observation, interview and psychological tests, providing individual or group counselling and designing behaviour-modification programmes.
roles.where: Clinical psychology (unit 6) — schizophrenia, mood, anxiety and OCD — with the abnormal-psychology-therapies and clinical-practice-and-ethics lessons, and research-methods test design from unit 5.

roles.title: Industrial-Organizational Psychologists
roles.what: Apply psychology to workplace problems — employee testing and selection, training and development, motivation and organisational analysis — to improve productivity and the work setting.
roles.where: Organisational psychology (unit 9) — motivation to work, leadership, group behaviour, work conditions and satisfaction — is the syllabus of the profession, sharpened by psychometric tests (unit 5).

roles.title: School Psychologists
roles.what: Diagnose and implement individual or schoolwide interventions for educational, behavioural and developmental issues, counselling students and families and consulting with school staff.
roles.where: The cognitive approach's development unit — Piaget to today — and Baron-Cohen's eyes test, with research-methods and psychometric tests (unit 5), ground the assessment and intervention design.

roles.title: Psychiatrists
roles.what: Diagnose, treat and help prevent mental disorders, bringing medical and pharmacological treatment together with a psychological understanding of the individual patient.
roles.where: The biological approach (unit 1) and clinical option (unit 6) — from brain-scan evidence to schizophrenia and mood disorders — give the medical model this career trains on, with ethics from unit 5.

roles.title: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
roles.what: Research conditions in local, regional, national and online markets — gathering data on consumers, competitors, prices and sales to judge a product's potential and plan advertising campaigns.
roles.where: Consumer psychology (unit 7) — decision-making, the product, advertising — and the unit 5 training in sampling, validity, reliability and data analysis are the analyst's core craft.
